cultivar: Fuding Dabai, Mingshan 131 and other approved cultivars
processing: A green tea whose detailed method is set out in a county standard. Little of it is publicly described; as with other Chinese greens, the leaf is fixed by heat, shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Little is documented for this tea; like other Sichuan greens, its prized picking comes in spring.
taste_profile: A rich chestnut aroma over a mellow body with a sweet aftertaste.

brewing.notes: General advice for a chestnut-scented green: slightly hotter water than for bud teas brings out the aroma, but keep steeps short.

vintage_note: Usual for a Chinese green: sold from the current year's harvest and best within the year, with spring tea the one to look for. Nothing suggests an ageing tradition.
description:
Qibei tea is a green from Xuanhan County in the northeast of Sichuan, named after Qibei township, which promoters call the tea village of eastern Sichuan. Its protected area takes in eight townships: Tuhuang, Fankuai, Qibei, Shitie, Dukou, Sandun, Qishu and Longquan.

The gardens grow established cultivars such as Fuding Dabai and Mingshan 131, rather than one local plant. Its method is fixed in a county standard, though few details of it circulate.

The character to expect is chestnut more than flowers: a warm rich aroma, a mellow body and a sweet finish, in a clear yellow-green cup. Slightly hotter water than you would use for a tender bud tea suits that style.

It is a regional tea, mostly sold in Sichuan. Look for the geographical indication mark and a recent harvest date.
history:
Little is documented about the tea before recent decades. In 2002 Xuanhan was named a quality tea base county by the provincial agriculture department, and Qibei a provincial model township for standardised tea growing.

A county standard for the tea dates from 2010, and national geographical indication protection followed on 26 September 2013.
